newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks halt slide on bargain-hunting, data.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks halt slide on bargain-hunting, data.

text.p: The Mexican bourse was still down in slow midday dealings on Thursday but had recouped some earlier losses, as foreign bargain hunters stepped in on cue from strong trade data.

"We're down but the market is calm, bottom-fishers step in each time it dips. Many prices began to pick up when the trade balance data came out," a floor trader said. The leading IPC share index was down 30.00 points, or 0.62 percent, at 4,806.49. The IPC had earlier reached as low as 4,793.99 on what dealers said was profit-taking after an extended record-breaking run.
Trading volume was much reduced from earlier sessions this week at 52.1 million shares.

The Finance Ministry announced mid-morning it had revised Mexico's trade surplus for May up to $220 million, from a preliminary figure of $88 million. Traders said the data alleviated fears the peso may no longer have been competitively priced for exporters.
Dealers said foreign buyers were tending to favor telecomms firm Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) and paper company Kimberly-Clark de Mexico.
Telmex had gained 20 centavos to 21.10 pesos, while paper company Kimberly-Clark Mexico was down 10 centavos at 37.00 pesos but had recovered from an earlier low of 36.85 pesos.
On the broad market, sliders outpaced gainers by 45 to 39.
